SELECTED_INDEX: 2
CONFIDENCE: 0.28
EXPLANATION: The dominant Raman line at 2117 cm⁻¹ fits the C≡C stretching of a terminal alkyne (2100–2140 cm⁻¹) and is too low for a nitrile (≈2220–2260 cm⁻¹).  Candidate 2 contains an alkyne but no nitrile, whereas candidates 1,3-6 carry nitrile groups that should give a band ≈2230 cm⁻¹ which is absent.  Additional features support an aliphatic alcohol in 2:  • strong C–H stretches at 2946, 2888, 2989 cm⁻¹ (tert-butyl groups);  • C–O stretch / C–C–O deformation of a tertiary alcohol near 1150 cm⁻¹;  • C–O–H related mode around 937 cm⁻¹;  • CH₃/CH₂ bending at 1454 cm⁻¹;  • skeletal deformations in the 670–700 cm⁻¹ region are common in small aliphatic alcohols.  Candidate 8 has only hydrocarbon modes and lacks the expected 1150 cm⁻¹ C–O band, while candidate 10 would require Si–H stretching near 2100 cm⁻¹, not present in the deuterated silane shown.  Hence candidate 2 best matches the observed Raman pattern.
